title: The Meridian Spine
hook_central: After bringing down the commissioner behind the Kessler collapse, forensic engineer Iris Kane accepts the flagship job of the reform built to prevent the next disaster — only to discover the reform itself is the instrument by which the people who financed Renn are capturing national infrastructure, protected by a name redacted from the one page she never recovered.

female.name: Iris Kane
tics: Thumbnail along edges reading for hairline cracks, escalating from reading documents as structures to reading institutions as structures built to fail on cue.
female.boundary: Will not sign a conclusion she cannot physically prove.
female.internal_voice: She mentally scans every system, document, and institution for hidden weaknesses before she accepts its function.

male.name: Stellan Marsh
male.voice: Charismatic statesman, speaks in national interest and legacy, always rational and measured.
tics: Adjusts cufflinks when confronted with inconvenient data
male.boundary: Never turns careless, always controls the frame, loses only because physical tool-mark is outside every registry he controls.
male.wound: His legacy — the Directorate — must survive at any cost; he betrays his own reform to preserve it.

supporting_cast.name: Petra Lund
supporting_cast.relation_type: lead materials certifier on Meridian Spine, former Kessler contractor
supporting_cast.secret: Used the same override method as Kessler to falsify load coupons; genuine copycat but guilty of her own act.

supporting_cast.name: Nadia Okafor
supporting_cast.secret: Steers Iris toward Halveston to burn the financier as the stopping point and shield Marsh; not for money but to preserve the Directorate.

supporting_cast.name: Gerald Halveston
supporting_cast.relation_type: chair of philanthropic infrastructure fund financing the Spine
supporting_cast.secret: Coordinated the capture project and moved the money to capture contracts; financed but did not architect; false answer 2.

supporting_cast.name: Aldous Renn
supporting_cast.relation_type: convicted mastermind of Kessler collapse, now prison source
supporting_cast.secret: Co-owner names redacted from the one page Iris never recovered; available only as source, not active mastermind.

central_mystery.question: Who built the post-Kessler reform into a national capture instrument — who are the co-owners behind Renn, and who architected using the correction itself to entrench the fraud at national scale?
central_mystery.answer: Stellan Marsh architected the National Integrity Directorate as a capture instrument: the reform built to prevent the next Kessler is the mechanism by which he and the co-owners who financed Renn now control national procurement, laundering the same fraud at the scale of a country behind the credibility of the body meant to stop it.

bloodline.description: No blood relation exists between Iris Kane and Stellan Marsh. Iris comes from working-class background, parents deceased. Stellan Marsh belongs to a political dynasty with no familial link to Iris.
hard_rules: Iris Kane and Stellan Marsh are not blood relatives.
Leads have no romantic or familial relationship.

world_rules: All evidence is physical (tool-marks, coupons, approval-timing); no confessions or monologues expose the truth.
Each tier – Lund, Okafor, Halveston, Marsh – is genuinely guilty of their own act; false answers are not mere frames but actual culprits.
Stellan Marsh never becomes careless, forgetful, or stupid (Rook-analog rule); his exposure comes only from a physical tool-mark outside every registry he controls.
The reform (National Integrity Directorate) is revealed as a capture instrument only from chapter 18; before that, no character can state it outright.
Marsh's role as architect is not named before chapter 19; before chapter 20, no statement that Marsh ordered or laundered the fraud.
The tool-mark proof is published exactly once, in chapter 21, after Marsh states his role on live record.
Chapter 13 partial release: tool-mark match Spine<->Kessler only — reopens certification, names no one.
Book 1 core sample is spent and cannot be reused as the winning card.
Single POV: Iris Kane holds all 22 chapters; third-person limited.
No romance subplot or explicit content; spice_level=1 ensures no sexual content.
No real people, real organizations, or real named agencies.
Aldous Renn remains convicted, not freed, not resurrected as active mastermind.
Reveals are assembled from physical evidence, never from a character's speech.

series_arc.thesis: A single irrefutable sample can bring down a corrupt system, but the victory grants the adversary a more elegant leash.
series_arc.ending_hook: Iris is celebrated as the whistleblower who took down the commissioner and immediately offered the role that ties her to the reform she does not yet see as a trap.

series_arc.thesis: The reform built to prevent disaster is the next disaster; the institution meant to stop fraud is the vehicle for its national scale.
series_arc.ending_hook: Iris resigns the Directorate and returns to the field, knowing that at least one co-owner name from the redacted page was never on any live record.

series_arc.thesis: The co-owner list is a rotating set of positions, not permanent identities; the real system is above any single name.
series_arc.ending_hook: Iris traces one position to a trust that legally does not exist, realizing the capture pattern is institutional.

series_arc.thesis: To break the capture, Iris must publish the full record — but publishing destroys the system's credibility beyond repair.
series_arc.ending_hook: She obtains the complete list but hesitates, weighing the cost of decertifying national infrastructure.

series_arc.thesis: The truth is worth the cost; Iris publishes the full record, accepts the collapse of the reform, and begins the true rebuilding from outside the institution.
series_arc.ending_hook: The series closes on Iris, outside the Directorate, teaching a new class of engineers to examine systems before they trust them.

content_rules: No explicit sexual content or romance subplot (spice level 1).
All interactions are consensual (professional, not romantic).
No real people, organizations, or identifiable agencies; all fictional.
